missionPremise: The five rails parcelGeometry, pipelines, railCorridor, etjStatus and landUseDescription stand open in all six counties with verdict excluded-mid-cutover (30 of the open cells) because RAIL_POLICY in scripts/six-county-completeness.mjs gives the mid-cutover class NO accept list at all — deliberately, while every other class has one (dispatch, Mission; scripts/six-county-completeness.mjs lines 80-85, self-test check 3). The program has never ruled whether the ledger is meant to become their source, so the block is open because nobody ruled, not because work is missing. The dispatch's consequent premise is that all five serve today from a non-ledger path and that a ruling therefore changes no customer outcome either way. THE RULING IS THE OPERATOR'S: this lane writes no store and changes no serving behaviour, and supplies the facts a ruling needs. Where that premise is false this close says so, because a ruling made on a false premise is the one failure mode the lane exists to prevent.
completionPredicate: For each of the five mid-cutover rails, establish from code and live reads (never from documents): (1) the exact serve path today, naming the service, function and store or upstream; (2) the ledger-cell state as one of empty / partially-written / written-and-unread, not collapsed; (3) the concrete cutover cost (which writer mints the atoms, the population, whether a vocabulary or contract change is implied); (4) what breaks if it never cuts over, naming the exception to the standing ledger-as-serving-path ruling and its cost in consistency; and (5) a recommendation of CUT OVER / STAYS ELSEWHERE / RETIRE with the serve path named. Plus at least two serve paths proven by violation (a read that fails or a value that disappears when the path is unavailable), one operator-runnable five-rail table, and one paragraph on which rails are ruled together and which needs its own decision. All of it met; the cited artifacts carry each item at the point of use.

Strongest single finding: etjStatus is the dispatch's high-value case and it inverts. P-296 IS the cutover on the authoritative path — cortex-api serves present for 48453:134392 (austin-tx:39) and a checked absent for 48209:97658 — and the CUSTOMER SURFACE serves the literal 'unresolved' for both, because the Property Explorer BFF replaces the whole cityLimitsFact and hardcodes the literal in composeCityLimits. Fixing the panel is independent of the ruling and should not wait for it.

Second finding, and the one that changes the ruling's framing: railCorridor is written-and-unserved. Rail-state classification needs three states, not two — 'written and unread' and 'written and unseen by any surface' are different costs, and the second implies the cutover ADDS a customer outcome. Any future mid-cutover verdict should say which of the three it means.

Method that worked: read the SERVING revision by image tag (gcloud run services list) then `git show <servingSha>:<path>` rather than reading HEAD; and read the customer surface by asset existence. A code read against HEAD would have shown the composer fix as if it were live.

The customer surface is directly comparable to cortex-api without any credential (both are public GETs), which is what made the ETJ three-way comparison possible from a seat with no store credential. Keep the cortex-api brokerage facets URL in the recon kit.
